chunks: Bakr al-Arqaṭ narrated to me from Abū ʿAbdillāh, or from Shuʿayb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

A man came in to him and said: “May Allah set you aright. I am a man devoted to you through my affection, and a severe need has afflicted me. I sought nearness through that with my household and my people, but it only increased me in distance from them.”
He عليه السلام said: “What Allah has given you is better than what He has taken from you.”
He said: “May I be your ransom, supplicate to Allah for me that He make me free of need from His creation.”

He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah apportions the sustenance of whomsoever He wills at the hands of whomsoever He wills. But ask Allah to make you free of the need that compels you toward the ignoble of His creation.”

key_terms.بِمَوَدَّتِي: through my love and affectionate loyalty
key_terms.حَاجَةٌ شَدِيدَةٌ: a severe state of need or hardship
key_terms.لِئَامِ: the ignoble or base among people
key_terms.مُنْقَطِعٌ: devoted and wholly attached in allegiance and affection
key_terms.يُغْنِيَكَ: to make you free of need

ai.seo_question: What should a believer ask Allah for when struggling with poverty and dependence on people?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that attachment to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام may bring worldly hardship, yet what Allah grants through that loyalty is better than what is lost. It also teaches proper du'a: rather than asking to be entirely independent of people, one should ask Allah to remove the degrading need that forces a person to turn to ignoble people.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Aban Bin Abdul Malik who said, ‘Bakr Al Arqat narrated to me, from Abu Abdullah,

(It has been narrated) from Shuayb, from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, that he went over to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> alone and he said, ‘May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Keep you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> well! I am a man who has been cut-off to you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> due to my cordiality and I have been hit by a severe need. I had approached with that to my family and my people but that did not increase me from them except for the distance’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So whatever Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> has Given you is better than what He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> has Taken from you’.
He said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Supplicate for me that He<sup>azwj</sup> Makes me to be needless from His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Distributes sustenance to whoever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to, upon the hands of the ones whom He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to. But, ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> Makes you to be self-sufficient from the needs which are making you desperate to the ignoble ones of His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Aban ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said that narrated to him Bakr ibn Arqat from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) or from Shu’ayb from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Once someone came to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and said, ‘May Allah keep you well, I am a man who devoutly loves you. I face a pressing need. I sought help from my family and tribe but it only has distanced me from them.’
The Imam said, ‘What Allah has given you is better than what He has taken from you.’
The man said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, pray for me to Allah so He will make me independent of His creatures.’

The Imam said, ‘Allah has assigned the sustenance of whomever He wanted to come through the hands of whomever He wanted, however, you can ask Allah to make you free of such needs that may force you to ask for help the ignoble ones of His creatures.’”
